Paul Pressler, former Texas judge and religious leader, accused of sexually assaulting teen for years

A lawsuit filed alleges that Paul Pressler, a former state judge, lawmaker and leader on the religious right, repeatedly sexually assaulted a young man over a period of decades, beginning when the boy was just 14.

The lawsuit alleges that Paul Pressler, a former justice on the 14th Court of Appeals who served in the Texas state house sexually assaulted Duane Rollins, his former bible study student, several times per month over a period of years. According to the filing, the abuse started in the late 1970s and continued less frequently after Rollins left Houston for college. Pressler denied allegation.

The abuse, which consisted of anal penetration, took place in Pressler’s master bedroom study, the suit alleges. Pressler told Rollins he was “special” and that the sexual contact was their God-sanctioned secret.

Pressler is a leading figure on the religious right in Texas and was a key player in the “conservative resurgence” of Southern Baptism. Pressler’s wife his former law partner Jared Woodfill, Woodfill Law Firm, Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary President Paige Patterson, Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary and First Baptist Church of Houston are also named as defendants in the suit.

Rollins seeks damages.

When asked about the suit, Ted Tredennick, Pressler’s attorney, pointed to Rollins' record, which is peppered with arrests on DUIs and other charges over the last several decades.

“Mr. Rollins is clearly a deeply troubled man, with a track record of multiple felonies and incarceration, and it is the height of irresponsibility that anyone would present such a bizarre and frivolous case — much less report on it,” Tredennick said.

Rollins and his lawyer, Daniel Shea, say his past legal troubles stemmed from behavior fueled by alcohol and drug addictions sparked by the childhood sexual abuse. In 1998, Rollins was jailed for 10 years on burglary charges. Pressler advocated for Rollins to receive parole in 2000, when he was first eligible, and then again in 2002. In his letter to the parole board, Pressler pledged to employ Rollins and be “personally involved in every bit of Duane’s life with supervision and control.”

Pressler previously settled with Rollins over a battery charge for an incident in a Dallas hotel room. That settlement is not public, Shea said, but reference is made to such an agreement in recent court filings.

Shea said that though Rollins filed that assault charge more than a decade ago, he had a “suppressed memory” of the sexual abuse until he made an outcry statement to a prison psychologist. A psychiatrist who has been working with Rollins wrote in a letter included in the suit that Rollins is a “reliable historian for the childhood sexual trauma to which he was repeatedly and chronically subjected.”

Pressler was President George H.W. Bush’s pick to lead the Office of Government Ethics but the administration ultimately ruled Pressler out after an FBI background investigation. News reports from the time suggest that Pressler was dismissed due to unspecified ethics issues.

Bonus Fish batter recipe.

1 egg milk - one splash flour - little bit depends on how much fish, just put a half inch or so in an appropriate size bowl or container and add more if needed. 1 small bag of potato chips(I like all dressed) but dill pickle or salt and vinegar or whatever the hell you like will work. Fish - enough to eat. oil, enough to fill the bottom of the pan a bit.

mix the egg and thesplash of milk and pour some more milk in a bowl. crush up the chips with a rolling pin or mug or something pour some flour in a bowl

Dip the fish in the milk then the flour and sit it to rest until it's all done and sitting and coated, then dip into the egg and then the chip crumbs again let it rest on a rack or paper towel or soemthing

Heat up some oil in a pan or use a deep fryer or whatever let it get nice n hot and fry up the fish.
